- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% if followed by a spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 3–8% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often underestimates — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% if sentiment turns neutral or bullish.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in the 1st–3rd day after a new sentiment shift — apply +1–3% bias to first 3 days post-sentiment change.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75% of recent high), model often fails to recognize — apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model tends to smooth too much — allow 1–2% volatility buffer in forecast for next 5 days.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike (e.g., -5%+ from peak), model often fails to anticipate — apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- Model often underestimates true price in the final 5–7 days of forecast horizon — apply +1–3% bias to last 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish or neutral.
